w_diff_split.definition: d_k = Y_k - Y_{k+1} on four equal windows (raw counts, no background subtraction); W = d_A^T K d_B; exact tridiagonal Poisson covariance; z_exact uses V_plug - tr(K S_A K S_B) floored at tr(K S_A K S_B)
w_diff_split.prior_art: Differencing at a fixed interval to cancel an unknown constant baseline is classical (Guggenheim 1926, Phil. Mag. 2, 538, doi 10.1080/14786442608564083; Kezdy-Swinbourne method). No novelty is claimed for differencing.
limitations: weight (1 - exp(-lam D)) ~ lam D for lam D << 1: slow components are suppressed with the background
spacing D was not pre-registered; D = 200 and D = 250 are both reported

split_protocol.full_stream: Even vs. odd 1-second macrotime blocks (independent halves A and B)
split_protocol.burst_gated_1ms: Alternating even vs. odd 1-ms burst index (independent halves A and B)
split_protocol.background_window: Bins 2200..3000 (800 bins during Red PIE window where Green donor excitation is dark)

caveats: In diffusing solution smFRET, fixed 1-ms time bins can slightly clip burst edges or include transit relaxation on high-FRET 1b.
Differencing across 4 windows multiplies each exponential weight by (1 - exp(-lam D)), reducing power at short D = 192-256 ps (1 - q ~ 0.06) vs. lifetime-matched D = 960-1200 ps (1 - q ~ 0.25-0.45).

dye_free_reference_pedestal_at_3600s.conclusion: The dye-free reference IRF trace exhibits a +1.91% post-pulse vs. pre-pulse baseline step (33.22 ppm of peak signal per bin) at T = 3600 s alongside the +2.62% step in the dye trace, confirming that the ~+2.3% baseline step is an instrument/TDC post-peak pedestal rather than multi-exponential dye kinetics, and explaining why 4-window W_diff,split cancels it cleanly.

assumptions: Stationary, ergodic, finite-state Markov channel; n independent identical channels; additive white measurement noise; current = sum of conductances.
W_C(t1,d) = C(t1) C(t1+2d) - C(t1+d)^2 on equally spaced lags; reversible => C completely monotone => W_C >= 0.
Filter (anti-aliasing) effects are not modelled here; lags must lie well beyond the filter time constant.
No experimental recording is analysed here. This is a simulation benchmark of the statistic.

reversible_null.note: min W/C(t2)^2 ~ 0 up to float error; sign constraint holds.

driven_cycle_real_spectrum.name: seeded search: strictly real spectrum, A>=6, slow rate 0.5-10/s, fast <=40/s

detection_time_gaussian_limit.method: Circulant-embedding Gaussian process with exact C(tau) from the rate matrix + white noise sigma_w; K=16 block U-statistic; jackknife SE
detection_time_gaussian_limit.caveat: Gaussian (many-channel) limit; finite-n non-Gaussianity, filtering, baseline drift and rundown are not modelled. z is signed: W_C < 0 gives negative z.

deduction_1_wronskian_sign_trichotomy.title: The Wronskian Sign Trichotomy for Linear Kinetic Topologies (Parallel W > 0 vs. Single-State W = 0 vs. Serial Cascade W < 0)
prior_art: Bateman 1910 (Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 15, 423-427: exact intermediate state convolution solution of serial radioactive decay chains)
Schoenberg 1951 (J. Analyse Math. 1, 331-374: Polya frequency functions PF_2 and log-concavity preservation under convolution)

identities.parallel_mixture: y_par(t) = c1 e^{-lam1 t} + c2 e^{-lam2 t} (c1,c2 > 0) => W(t) = +c1 c2 (lam1 - lam2)^2 e^{-(lam1+lam2)t} > 0 and W_diff(t0,D) > 0 for all t, t0 >= 0
identities.single_state: y_mono(t) = c1 e^{-lam1 t} + b => W(t) = 0 and W_diff(t0,D) = 0 identically
identities.serial_cascade: 1 -> 2 -> 3 with y_ser(t) = c (e^{-lam1 t} - e^{-lam2 t}) + b => W(t) = -c^2 (lam1 - lam2)^2 e^{-(lam1+lam2)t} < 0 and W_diff(t0,D) = -c^2 a1 a2 (e^{-lam1 D} - e^{-lam2 D})^2 e^{-(lam1+lam2)t0} < 0 for ALL t, t0 >= 0 (including post-peak tail t0 > t_peak where dy_ser/dt < 0)

deduction_2_closed_form_rate_dispersion_.title: Closed-Form Zero-Fit Rate-Dispersion Estimator sigma_hat_lambda(t0, D)
prior_art: Koppel 1972 (J. Chem. Phys. 57, 4814-4820, doi:10.1063/1.1678153: method of cumulants in dynamic light scattering)

definitions.cumulant_bridge: W(t0,D)/a_2^2 = D^2 Var_p(lambda) * (sinh(Delta_lambda D / 2) / (Delta_lambda D / 2))^2 = D^2 sigma_lambda,p^2 + O(D^4)

deduction_3_hankel_turan_3x3_spectral_ra.title: The 3x3 Higher-Order Hankel-Turan Determinant (H_3,diff) — Model-Free Spectral Rank Ladder (M=1 vs. M=2 vs. M>=3)
prior_art: Karlin 1968 (Total Positivity, Vol. I, Stanford Univ. Press: Hankel determinants of completely monotone / Laplace-Stieltjes transforms)
Prony 1795 (J. Ecole Polytech. 1, 24-76: exponential rank and Hankel singularity)
deduction_3_hankel_turan_3x3_spectral_ra.cauchy_binet_identity: H_{r,diff} = sum_{1<=m1<...<mr<=M_exp} c_tilde_{m1}...c_tilde_{mr} prod_{i<j} (e^{-lam_{mi} D} - e^{-lam_{mj} D})^2
deduction_3_hankel_turan_3x3_spectral_ra.step_down_testing_rule: Under M_exp = 1, rank(M_3) = 1 so the 2x2 cofactor matrix adj(M_3) vanishes identically; therefore H_3,diff is evaluated as a step-down test conditioned on H_2,diff = W_diff > 0 (where rank(M_3) >= 2 and adj(M_3) != 0 under H_0^(2): M_exp = 2).
